lens:
Risk management and portfolio construction. The fear model is used only for what it is validated for: forecasting risk. Its risk outputs are regime-adjusted volatility (sigma combined with P_calm, P_stressed and P_panic), q_next, breadth and M_pct, and the systemic-day label. None of it is used as a return forecast.

Three families, ranked by expected usefulness to the selection:
- **R2, shock-typed exits.** A stop-loss policy: sell after a stock's idiosyncratic hit, hold through a systemic one. It has the best power, with about 250 idiosyncratic events in dev spread over 77 distinct weeks. The hindsight universe biases it AGAINST passing, so a pass would be credible.
- **R1, fear-gated exposure overlay on the equal-weight basket.** Only about 5 market episodes in dev, so power is low. I recommend adopting it under risk-forecast and non-inferiority tests rather than spending a Holm slot.
- **R3, risk-timed, staggered re-entry after systemic hits.** Its events are clustered in time, and the universe bias runs IN ITS FAVOR. If another lens declares a reversal family, merge R3 into it.

Design facts found from signal columns only. I read x, Z, q_next, P_* and M_pct from outputs/v3 and opened no prices and no returns:
- **The per-stock regime multiplier barely moves when averaged over the basket.** From the 5th percentile to the maximum in 2024-25 it spans 0.93-1.09 of its stationary level at a 10-session horizon, and 0.84-1.57 at 1 session. An inverse-multiplier exposure rule would therefore average 0.98-0.99, which is useless. Basket risk has to come from M_pct/breadth, which capture commonality, and from the basket's own realized-volatility level.
- **Market stress is rare and short.** There are 5 episodes with M_pct ≥ 1.5 (1 in 2024, 4 in 2025), and runs at that level have a median length of 2 sessions over 2023-26. Stock hits (x ≥ 3 and Z ≥ 2) are many: in dev, about 250 idiosyncratic and 730 systemic.

Direction of the universe bias, for reading every lens's results:
- The universe was selected as 2026 AI winners. A name that dipped and never recovered is not on that list.
- That inflates buy-the-dip and momentum backtests.
- It deflates stop, avoid and low-risk tilts.

families.name: R2 Shock-typed exits: sell after idiosyncratic (information) hits, hold through systemic (liquidity) hits
families.mechanism:
A stop-loss adds value only if returns keep going the same way after the trigger. Under a random walk or reversal it destroys value (Kaminski & Lo 2014; Lo & Remorov 2017).

The fear model's day-type label predicts which way returns go:
- Firm-specific information shocks drift (Bernard & Thomas 1989; Chan 2003; Savor 2012).
- Market-wide, liquidity-driven selloffs revert (Campbell, Grossman & Wang 1993; Llorente, Michaely, Saar & Wang 2002; Nagel 2012).

So the family is a typed stop: exit after a stock's idiosyncratic hit, hold through a systemic one.

The exit keys on shock type, not on q_next. After idiosyncratic shocks the model's own tail forecast already overstates next-day risk (F5: observed/forecast 0.67), so an exit driven by q_next would over-trade. What remains after such shocks is drift, not tail risk.
families.entry_rule:
At the close of t, stock i is 'hit' when both hold:
- x_{i,t} ≥ 3: the low was at least 3 own-sigma below the previous close.
- Z_{i,t} ≥ 2: fear is acute or worse.

Day t is systemic if at least 10% of eligible stocks have x ≥ 2, otherwise idiosyncratic (the F5 label).

The exit trigger is an idiosyncratic hit in V1, V2 and V4, and any hit in V3. A new trigger during an exclusion window restarts the window.
families.execution:
- Sell at the open of t+1 (one-day-delay test: the open of t+2).
- Spread the proceeds pro rata over the other basket names. Strategy and benchmark both stay fully invested, so the test is purely cross-sectional, with no market timing.
- When the window ends, re-buy to the current equal weight at the open.
- The basket resets to equal weight on the first session of each month.
- Costs are charged on all four legs: about 0.4% of the excluded weight per event at 10 bps, and 1.0% at 25 bps.
- Live, the same rule governs single-name holdings: sell, and the proceeds go to cash or the next trade.
families.exit_rule:
Re-admission depends on the variant:
- V1: after 20 sessions.
- V2: after 60 sessions.
- V3: after 20 sessions.
- V4: at the first full session with Z < 1.0 after at least 5 sessions, capped at 60.

In V1, V2 and V4, systemic hits trigger nothing: hold, and there is no price stop.
variants: V2 Idiosyncratic hit, exclusion 60 sessions (PEAD horizon)
V3 Untyped stop (mechanism foil): any hit, systemic or idiosyncratic, exclusion 20 sessions
V4 Idiosyncratic hit, re-admit at the first full session with Z < 1.0 after >= 5 sessions (cap 60)
families.benchmark:
The buy-and-hold equal-weight basket: fully invested, with the same monthly reset.

Primary statistic: the mean of d_t = r_strategy,t − r_basket,t, net of costs. Its standard error comes from HAC (Newey-West with lag equal to the window length) or a stationary bootstrap with mean block equal to the window length.

The equivalent event form is the date-weighted mean of (r_rest − r_i) over each window.

Checks: a beta-adjusted version (r_i − β̂_i·r_B, with β̂_i estimated over the trailing 126 sessions) and a same-stock random-day baseline.
families.predicted_signature:
1. V1 > 0. Excluded names underperform the rest of the basket, and the shortfall accrues gradually (at most 1/3 of it in the first 2 sessions), as drift would rather than a one-day effect.
2. Typed beats untyped: V1 − V3 > 0. The systemic-hit exits inside V3 lose money, because those names out-rebound the basket (liquidity reversal).
3. Dose-response: events with x ≥ 4 show a larger shortfall than events with 3 ≤ x < 4.
4. At least 2/3 of the gain survives the one-day delay, and the gain survives beta adjustment.
5. If V2 ≥ V1, the daily shortfall rate decays across the 60 sessions, like post-earnings drift.
families.expected_events_2024_2025:
Counts from v3 in-sample signals; point-in-time refits will differ slightly.
- V1, V2 and V4: about 253 idiosyncratic hits in dev, on 147 dates, 77 distinct weeks and 100 tickers. They are nearly independent in time.
- V3 adds about 732 systemic hits on 108 dates.
- 2026 holdout: about 77 idiosyncratic hits. The standard error there is about 1.5%, which is enough for a sign check but weak.

Power:
- The standard error of the mean 20-session excess is about 0.8-1.0%, so a true 1% shortfall clears 1 standard error.
- Holm across 8-12 families needs t ≈ 2.3-2.5, which means a shortfall of about 2-2.5%.
- Estimated P(pass full gate) ≈ 15-25%.
- The bias runs against this family, so a pass would be credible.
families.options_expression:
The default is to sell the shares, which is the cheapest exit.

If the holder must keep them (taxes, or a core position):
- Write a 30-45 DTE covered call at about 0.30 delta through the window, but only when VR = IV30 / annualized σ̂_fear(21) ≥ 1.25. After earnings, IV usually collapses, so this will be rare.
- Buy a protective put only if VR ≤ 0.90.

Do not buy puts as a standalone bearish bet. An expected drift of 1-2% over 20 sessions is small next to a 30-45 DTE put's spread (3-10% of premium) and its delta-scaled payoff. Options rarely beat shares here.
families.main_risks:
- Post-earnings and news drift has largely disappeared in large, liquid stocks since the mid-2000s (Chordia, Goyal, Sadka, Sadka & Shivakumar 2009; Martineau 2022). The shortfall may be about zero for the mega-caps.
- The hindsight universe under-represents names that kept falling after their own bad news. That biases results against the family: conservative, but it costs power.
- Each event moves only 1/N of the basket, so even a real effect matters mostly for concentrated books.
- An earnings miss on a broad down day is typed systemic, so its exit is missed.
- Four-leg costs need a shortfall of at least about 1% to survive costs ×2.5.
- Likely overlap with 'avoid falling knives' rules from other lenses. Merge them rather than count the same idea twice in Holm.

families.name: R1 Fear-gated exposure overlay on the equal-weight AI basket (conditional volatility targeting, de-risk only)
families.mechanism:
Volatility clusters, but short-horizon expected returns do not rise in proportion to variance. So cutting exposure when forecast risk is high raises risk-adjusted returns (Fleming, Kirby & Ostdiek 2001; Moreira & Muir 2017; Harvey et al. 2018). The effect is stronger with a downside-risk measure (Wang & Yan 2021) and when exposure moves only in extreme states (Bongaerts, Kang & van Dijk 2020).

Out of sample the gains are fragile:
- Real-time versions often fail to beat buy-and-hold (Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang & Yan 2020).
- The usual in-sample scaling constant is a look-ahead (Liu, Tang & Zhou 2019).
- De-risking misses V-shaped rebounds.
- The market-level version survives trading costs best (Barroso & Detzel 2021).

The fear model supplies the timing. M_pct is a breadth thermometer of downside regimes, validated against VXN, and the stock-level stressed regime persists about 14 sessions.

Design answers to the critique:
- A causal target (an expanding median), so no in-sample constant.
- No leverage: E ≤ 1.
- A floor: E ≥ 0.25.
- Conditional, fear-gated action.
- Staggered re-entry.
- Half-day sessions are ignored.

The target comes from M_pct and from the basket's own HAR+M volatility forecast, not from averaging stock regimes, because that average barely moves.
families.entry_rule:
At the close of each full session t (half-days: hold the current exposure), compute a target exposure E_t in [0.25, 1] for the equal-weight basket of all eligible stocks.

The de-risk state switches on at the first close with M_pct_t ≥ 1.5.
- V1: E = 0.5 when the state switches on.
- V2: inside the state, E_t = clip(σ*_t/σ̂_t, 0.25, 1).
- V3 and V4 have no state. Every session, E_t = clip(σ*_t/σ̂_t, 0.25, 1) for V3, or clip((σ*_t/σ̂_t)², 0.25, 1) for V4.

Definitions:
- σ̂_t is the recursive HAR+M forecast of the basket's next-5-session realized vol. This is the repo's v3-2 design: OLS of log forward 5-session realized vol on the HAR lags and M, re-estimated each day on rows s ≤ t−5 from 2023-07, with at least 60 rows.
- σ*_t is the median of σ̂_s over s ≤ t, a causal target.
families.execution:
- Orders go in at the open of t+1 (one-day-delay test: t+2). Every basket name is scaled pro rata to E_t.
- The remainder is held as cash earning 0% in the test, which is conservative.
- Constituents reset to equal weight on the first session of each month, for strategy and benchmark alike.
- V3 and V4 trade only when |E_target − E_held| ≥ 0.10.
- Costs: 10 bps per side on traded notional, with stress tests at 25 bps and costs ×2.5.
families.exit_rule:
- **V1:** E holds at 0.5 while M_pct ≥ 1.0. On each full session with M_pct < 1.0, E rises by 0.25 (0.5, then 0.75, then 1.0). A new close with M_pct ≥ 1.5 resets E to 0.5.
- **V2:** the state ends at the first full session with M_pct < 1.0. E then rises by 0.25 per session to 1, using the same staircase as V1.
- **V3 and V4:** continuous.

No price stops and no time limit.
variants: V1 Staircase, pure fear: E = 0.5 at M_pct >= 1.5; +0.25 per full session with M_pct < 1.0 until 1.0
V2 Fear-gated vol target: inside the state (on at M_pct >= 1.5, off at the first full session with M_pct < 1.0) E = clip(σ*/σ̂_HAR+M, 0.25, 1); staircase back to 1
V3 Always-on inverse-vol target: E = clip(σ*/σ̂_HAR+M, 0.25, 1), 0.10 no-trade band
V4 Always-on inverse-variance target (Moreira-Muir form): E = clip((σ*/σ̂_HAR+M)^2, 0.25, 1), 0.10 no-trade band
families.benchmark:
A static mix of the same equal-weight basket and cash, at the variant's own average exposure Ē over the evaluation window. Holding less of a rising basket is then neither rewarded nor penalized.

Primary per-session statistic, compatible with SPA: d_t = u(r_strategy,t) − u(Ē·r_basket,t), where u(r) = r − (γ/2)·r² and γ = 5. Results at γ = 2 and γ = 10 are reported. The standard error comes from HAC or a stationary bootstrap.

Secondary:
- Sharpe-ratio difference against holding 100% of the basket (Ledoit & Wolf 2008).
- CVaR95 and maximum drawdown at matched exposure.
families.predicted_signature:
1. The gain is in the variance term. Strategy variance is at least 15% below the static mix's, while the timing-of-mean term, mean((E_t − Ē)·r_t), is indistinguishable from zero. No return skill is claimed.
2. Moreira-Muir: the basket's realized return per unit of realized variance is lower on sessions with E < 1 than on sessions with E = 1.
3. The gain comes from multi-week stressed episodes. Single-spike, V-shaped episodes contribute zero or less.
4. Persistence: the one-day delay keeps at least 2/3 of the gain.
5. Fear gating helps: V2 ≥ V3, i.e. conditional targeting beats always-on targeting.
families.expected_events_2024_2025:
V1, from v3 in-sample signals, with no returns read:
- 5 de-risk episodes (1 in 2024, 4 in 2025).
- About 62 sessions at reduced exposure (8 in 2024, 54 in 2025).
- 15 exposure changes.
- Mean exposure 0.985 in 2024 and 0.90 in 2025.

V2-V4: roughly 20-60 rebalances a year. 2026 holdout: about 4 episodes and 39 reduced sessions.

Power is low:
- Assumed daily basket vol: about 1.8% in calm and 3.5% in stress.
- On that assumption, the variance gain is about 3-5% a year of certainty-equivalent return at γ = 5.
- Noise from mistimed stress-day returns has a standard error of about 6-10% a year, so the expected t is about 0.4-0.8.
- Estimated P(pass full gate with Holm) ≈ 10%.

Recommendation: do not spend a Holm slot on R1. Adopt it as a risk overlay if all three hold:
- the risk forecasts pass VaR and QLIKE tests;
- the certainty-equivalent return is non-inferior (at least −0.5 standard errors against the static mix);
- CVaR95 and drawdown are lower.

Otherwise, keep only the framework's volatility and stress caps.
families.options_expression:
When the overlay cuts exposure and VR = IV30 / annualized σ̂_fear(21) ≥ 1.25 on the most liquid holdings (MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, AVGO, AMD, TSM, ORCL):
- Cut delta by writing 30-45 DTE covered calls at about 0.30-0.40 delta instead of selling shares. This keeps upside up to the strike in a V-shaped rebound, which is the overlay's main failure mode, and harvests the elevated IV (Whaley 2002; Israelov & Nielsen 2015).
- Re-enter with 21-35 DTE cash-secured puts at about 0.25-0.30 delta on the same names.

If VR < 1.25, use shares.

No protective puts. In stress they are bought at peak IV; in calm, spreads across 134 names cost more than they save.

Options beat shares here only when IV is rich relative to the fear forecast. There is no historical IV to test this, so the options version is paper-test only.
families.main_risks:
- Few independent episodes: 5 in dev.
- V-shaped rebounds. The best and worst days cluster in the same stressed weeks, so de-risking a day late sells the low (Cederburg et al. 2020).
- The fear reading needs dips to register, so it lags the onset of stress.
- The HAR target drifts with the sample.
- The hindsight universe makes any reduction in exposure look worse on raw return. The static-mix benchmark neutralizes this.
- Half-day sessions read quiet and must not trigger re-entry; 2026-11-27 was one.
- The verdict depends on γ, which is a preference, not a fact. It is pre-declared at 5.

families.name: R3 Risk-timed, staggered re-entry after systemic hits (liquidity provision with entry-variance control)
families.mechanism:
In broad selloffs, liquidity suppliers' capital is constrained. Prices of the hardest-hit names overshoot and then revert over days to weeks, and the premium for providing liquidity rises with market stress (Campbell, Grossman & Wang 1993; Brunnermeier & Pedersen 2009; Nagel 2012; Hendershott & Menkveld 2014).

The risk-management element is when to enter. The panic regime has about 2.4 times the stressed regime's daily scale (3.76 against 1.56 own-sigma). But it lasts only about 1.7 sessions, with a 58% daily chance of exiting to stressed or calm. Waiting until P_panic decays, or entering in tranches, should cut entry variance by more than it cuts expected return. Price stops are counterproductive for reversal trades (Kaminski & Lo 2014).
families.entry_rule:
A setup at the close of t needs:
- a systemic day: at least 10% of eligible stocks have x ≥ 2;
- stock i hit: x_{i,t} ≥ 3 and Z_{i,t} ≥ 2;
- at most one setup per stock in 10 sessions.

Entry depends on the variant:
- **V1 and V4:** buy at the open after the first close t' in [t, t+5] with P_panic,i,t' < 0.20. If P_panic stays at or above 0.20 for all 5 sessions, there is no trade, because a persistent panic is not a pure liquidity shock.
- **V2:** buy a third at each of the opens of t+1, t+2 and t+3.
- **V3:** buy all at the open of t+1.
families.execution:
- Long shares at the open. In the delay test, each tranche moves one session later.
- Each trade is sized for equal risk: notional proportional to 1/σ̂_i(H), the regime-adjusted volatility from the framework.
- Each setup date gets equal total risk, so a 40-name selloff counts as one event.
- Funded from cash.
- Costs: 10 bps per side, with stress tests at 25 bps and costs ×2.5.
families.exit_rule:
Time stop only. V1-V3 sell at the open 20 sessions after the first entry; V4 sells after 5 sessions.

No price stop. A new idiosyncratic hit on a held name triggers the R2 exit.
variants: V1 Risk-timed single entry: open after the first close within 5 sessions with P_panic < 0.20; hold 20
V2 Staggered thirds at opens t+1, t+2, t+3; exit at open t+21
V3 Immediate single entry at open t+1; hold 20 (un-timed foil)
V4 Risk-timed entry as V1; hold 5 (liquidity-reversal horizon)
families.benchmark:
Primary: beta-adjusted excess over the equal-weight basket in each trade window, r_i − β̂_i·r_B. Here β̂_i is the OLS beta of daily returns on the basket over the 126 sessions before the setup. The excess is aggregated into a daily sleeve series, with equal risk per trade and equal weight per setup date.

Why beta-adjust: the hardest-hit names in a broad selloff have high beta. A raw basket excess would score a market rebound in a bull sample as alpha.

The excess must also be ≥ 0 against both:
- the raw equal-weight basket;
- the same stock bought on random eligible days in 2024-25.
families.predicted_signature:
1. Beta-adjusted excess > 0, concentrated in sessions 1-10, so V4 keeps at least half of V1's excess.
2. Dose-response: the excess is larger for higher I_{i,t} (fear relative to the cross-section) and on days with M_pct ≥ 1.5, since the liquidity premium rises with market stress (Nagel 2012).
3. Risk timing works: V1 and V2 have a lower per-trade standard deviation than V3 with a similar mean, so their information ratio is at least V3's.
4. It mirrors R2: systemic-hit names outperform where idiosyncratic-hit names underperform.
families.expected_events_2024_2025:
From v3 in-sample signals:
- About 732 setups in dev, on about 108 systemic dates that form about 25 selloff clusters.
- Effective N is about 25-60.
- The standard error of the date-weighted 20-session excess is about 1-1.5%, so the minimum detectable effect is about 1.5-2%.
- 2026 holdout: about 313 setups.

Estimated P(pass full gate with Holm) ≈ 10-15%, and the universe bias runs in this family's favor.

Recommendation: if another lens declares a reversal family for systemic dips, fold V1 and V2 into it as execution variants instead of spending a separate Holm slot.
families.options_expression:
During the panic window, when IV is rich (VR = IV30 / annualized σ̂_fear(21) ≥ 1.25):
- Sell 21-35 DTE cash-secured puts with strike ≈ spot × (1 − 0.5·σ̂_i(1)·√DTE), sized to the equity notional.
- You are paid to wait, and assignment becomes a staggered entry at a discount.

After the panic subsides (the V1 timing) and VR ≤ 1.0:
- Use shares, or 45-60 DTE calls at about 0.5 delta for defined risk.
- The maximum loss is the premium, and no stop is needed.

Options beat shares when IV is rich (cash-secured puts), or when a hard loss cap is wanted without a stop (calls). Option P/L cannot be backtested, because there is no historical IV. The roughly 30 expired-contract samples can only spot-check pricing.
families.main_risks:
- Hindsight universe bias in this family's favor: a name that dipped and never recovered is not on a 2026 AI-winners list. That inflates both dev and 2026 results, so the beta-adjusted and same-stock checks must be required.
- The exploratory event study (buying at Z ≥ 2.5, with both shock types mixed) found no reliable edge in 2023-25, a period that overlaps this dev window. The prior is weak, even though the typed split comes from mechanism.
- Liquidity reversal in large caps is fast (1-2 sessions), so waiting (V1) may forgo it. That is why V3 is kept as the foil.
- The systemic label fires on about 25% of sessions. Many setups will be ordinary down days with little liquidity stress.
- Events are clustered, leaving few effective observations.
- Gap risk at the open after a panic close.

position_sizing_and_risk:
**1) Risk tools are validated as forecasts, not as alpha.**
Every trade is sized with one risk model: regime-adjusted volatility, q_next, and correlation driven by breadth. That model is judged by tests that have power:
- VaR coverage (Kupiec 1995; Christoffersen 1998), for the equal-weight basket and for random 10-name books in 2024-25.
- QLIKE loss against EWMA(0.94) and against 21-session realized volatility (Patton 2011).

Use the regime-adjusted volatility if its QLIKE loss is within 1 standard error of EWMA's and it passes 95% and 99% VaR coverage. Otherwise size with EWMA. Only alpha families spend SPA and Holm budget.

**2) Risk units.**
- **Stock volatility.** The forecast standard deviation of an H-session return is σ̂_i(H) = sigma_{i,t} × sqrt(Σ_{j=1..H} (p_{i,t}·A^j)·s²). Here p = (P_calm, P_stressed, P_panic) at the close, and A and s come from the point-in-time refit. By the reflection principle, s_k is regime k's daily scale in own-sigma units.
- **Shrinkage.** Before use, shrink each stock's log regime multiplier halfway toward that day's cross-sectional mean. q_next's within-day calibration slope on dev is 0.50, meaning the model spreads stocks about twice too far apart.
- **Correlation.** Use an equicorrelation ρ_t equal to the larger of the 63-session and 21-session average pairwise correlations of eligible names. It rises quickly in stress (Longin & Solnik 2001; Ang & Chen 2002).

**3) Book limits.** NAV is account equity. No margin, long-only shares, level-2 options.
- **Cash.** Share notional + cash-secured-put strike notional + long-option premium ≤ 100% of NAV. Net delta ≤ 100% of NAV.
- **Volatility.** Ex-ante book volatility ≤ 30% annualized. This binds mainly in stress, so it is conditional de-risking as a risk preference, with no alpha claim.
- **Stress.** One-day systemic stress loss ≤ 10% of NAV. In the scenario, every share position falls 3·σ̂_i(1) at once (ρ = 1, the q_next event in every name). Long options lose at most their premium; cash-secured puts lose their intrinsic value at the stressed price.
- **Per name.** ≤ 10% of NAV, or ≤ 5% if q_next ≥ 0.10 or P_panic ≥ 0.5 at entry.
- **Per segment.** ≤ 30%. Compute chips, foundry/memory and semicap together ≤ 45%.
- **Liquidity.** A position ≤ 1% of 20-day average daily volume. Exclude names whose 20-day median dollar volume is under $20M.
- **Options.**
  - Long premium per trade ≤ the smaller of the trade's risk budget (RB) and 1% of NAV, and ≤ 4% of NAV in total.
  - Cash-secured-put notional ≤ 10% of NAV per name and ≤ 40% in total.
  - Covered calls only against shares held.
- **Sleeves.**
  - An optional core AI basket = K × E_t. K is the user's strategic weight (default 60% of NAV); E_t comes from R1 if R1 is adopted, otherwise 1.
  - The tactical sleeve (all alpha families) ≤ 12% annualized ex-ante risk, and ≤ 6% per family.

**4) Fractional Kelly with shrinkage toward zero edge.** For each adopted family:
- **Point estimate.** IR̂ = mean ÷ standard deviation of the per-trade excess return, net of base costs, from dev plus 2026.
- **Standard error.** se = 1/√N_eff. N_eff is the number of distinct entry weeks, or distinct selloff clusters for systemic-event families.
- **Prior.** IR ~ N(0, 0.05²). The prior is tight on purpose: H5 failed, the panic-buy edge flipped sign, the sample is two years, and many families are being tested.
- **Posterior.** IR_post = IR̂ × 0.05² / (0.05² + se²).
- **Risk budget.** RB is the one-standard-deviation loss over the holding period, in % of NAV: RB = min(tier cap, c·IR_post), with c = 1/4. When n trades of the same family open within 5 sessions, divide RB by 1 + (n−1)ρ. This is the joint-Kelly correction for correlated bets; ρ = ρ_t for systemic-event families and 0.3 for idiosyncratic ones.
- **Notional.** Notional = RB / σ̂_i(H). Use total rather than excess volatility, because beta cannot be hedged.
- **Worked example.** IR̂ = 0.15 on N_eff = 80 gives se = 0.11 and IR_post ≈ 0.025, so RB ≈ 0.6% of NAV. With σ̂_i(20) = 18%, the notional is about 3.5% of NAV.
- **No equity premium.** It never counts as edge in tactical sizing; otherwise the hindsight-biased drift would leak back in.
- **Why a quarter of Kelly.** The chance of ever losing half the capital is 0.5^(2/c−1): 50% at full Kelly, 12.5% at half, 0.8% at a quarter (Thorp 2006; MacLean, Thorp & Ziemba 2011). Full Kelly on estimated edges over-bets (MacLean, Ziemba & Blazenko 1992).
- **Updating.** Re-estimate IR_post every quarter from paper and live trades as N_eff grows.

**5) Conviction tiers.** Caps on RB per trade:
- **Tier 0, paper or log only.** The family was not adopted, or 2026 disagrees in sign.
- **Tier 1, pilot, ≤ 0.25% of NAV.** Passed the dev gate (1 standard error, SPA plus Holm, mechanism signature, costs ×2.5, one-day delay). 2026 has the same sign but t < 1, or fewer than 20 effective events.
- **Tier 2, standard, ≤ 0.5%.** 2026 agrees with t ≥ 1 on its own.
- **Tier 3, high conviction, ≤ 1.0%.** Tier 2, plus all of:
  - today's trigger clears the fear model's 90% bootstrap band (Z_lo ≥ 2 for stock triggers, M_pct_lo ≥ 1.5 for R1);
  - the reading is not from a half-day;
  - there are no earnings inside the holding window (checked live against the Robinhood earnings calendar);
  - the family is not flagged in the paper test.
- **Demotion.** A family drops one tier when its rolling 40-trade live or paper excess is below −1 standard error. Two demotions send it to Tier 0 pending review.

**6) Stops.**
- No price stops on reversal or liquidity-provision entries. Stops add value only when returns are positively autocorrelated (Kaminski & Lo 2014; Lo & Remorov 2017), and the panic regime mean-reverts in about 2 sessions.
- The only exits are:
  - pre-declared time stops;
  - typed exits (R2: out after idiosyncratic information shocks, hold through systemic ones);
  - long options, when a hard loss cap is wanted.
- No price-based stop on the core beta; R1 is the response there.
- A model-risk brake applies to the tactical sleeve only:
  - a sleeve drawdown of 8% of NAV halves every RB;
  - at 12%, no new tactical trades are opened, open ones run to their time exits, and the family set is reviewed;
  - normal budgets return when the drawdown is back under 4%, or after 60 sessions with a documented review.

**7) Execution.**
- Signals are computed at the close and orders go in at the next open.
- **Shares:** marketable limits capped at 0.5·σ̂_i(1) beyond the prior close, so gaps are not chased.
- **Options:**
  - Place limits at the mid and improve by no more than 25% of the spread.
  - Skip if the spread is more than 10% of the mid or open interest is under 500.
- **Half-days** (for example 2026-11-27) read artificially quiet.
  - Never re-risk or re-admit on a half-day reading.
  - Keep the prior targets and size from the last full session.
- **Options versus shares.** Define VR = IV_30d ÷ annualized σ̂_i(21).
  - Sell premium (cash-secured puts or covered calls) only if VR ≥ 1.25.
  - Buy premium (calls or puts) only if VR ≤ 0.90.
  - Otherwise trade shares.
  - Single-stock options carry little variance premium on average, so act only on large gaps (Driessen, Maenhout & Vilkov 2009; Goyal & Saretto 2009).
- **Earnings.** No short-dated option across an earnings date unless the trade is about the earnings.
- **Testing.** There is no historical IV, so the options rules are paper-test only, spot-checked on the roughly 30 expired-contract samples.
